technical-summary: Fixed provider CLI probes failing with WinError 2 on Windows. Root cause: probes ran a bare argv list (subprocess.run(["opencode","--version"])) which CreateProcess cannot use to launch npm/pip .CMD shims. Added shared adapters/probe.py with run_cli() (shell-routes on Windows, direct exec on POSIX) and probe_cli_version() (which-resolve + run + correct available flag). Refactored opencode and openhands probes to use probe_cli_version (also fixed their except handler that returned available=True on failure). Routed copilot, qwen, and roo subprocess calls through run_cli (preserving their present-on-PATH availability semantics). Added regression tests covering missing executable, spawn failure -> available False, success/nonzero exit, cross-platform run_cli, a win32-only .CMD shim test proving bare list fails while run_cli succeeds, and opencode delegation to the shared helper. All 7 new tests + existing provider unit suite pass; ruff clean.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed provider CLIs (opencode and others) reporting WinError 2 on Windows by running their version probes through the shell so npm-installed .CMD shims resolve correctly.

technical-summary: Validated all providers in Docker and added a cross-provider probe contract test. Confirmed the default probe _probe_cli (registry.py) resolves the full executable via shutil.which before running, so it is unaffected by the Windows .CMD bug; the continue and pi custom probes do not spawn subprocess (which-check / file-check). Added tests/unit/providers/test_provider_probe_contract.py: parametrized over every PATH-based provider probe, stubs shutil.which to None and asserts _probe_provider_cli returns available=False with executable=None — guarding the whole class of bug (probe crash or masking failure as available) across all providers on any platform. 14 tests pass; full provider unit suite green; ruff clean.

technical-summary: Wired pi-lens LSP support into the coding-lsp enable flow. Added an optional on_lsp_enabled hook to ProviderDescriptor: a provider-declared capability fired when coding-lsp is enabled so the provider can provision its own LSP support. coding_lsp_bootstrap._on_enabled now calls a new language_servers_sync.provision_provider_lsp_support() that fans out to each descriptor's on_lsp_enabled (best-effort, failures logged not fatal). The pi adapter implements _pi_ensure_lens, which runs `<pi-bin> install npm:pi-lens` via resolve_agent_bin (skips if the pi harness is absent, idempotent). pi-lens auto-discovers language servers from PATH, so no per-language config writer is needed — the server binaries installed by enable_language are sufficient. Providers that self-provide LSP (language_servers_config OR on_lsp_enabled set) are now excluded from the generic ag-lsp MCP projection in sync_generic_lsp_mcp_to_providers, so pi gets pi-lens instead of the redundant ag-lsp MCP server (and any previously-synced ag-lsp entry is pruned). Added 5 unit tests covering the pi hook (skip/install paths), generic-MCP exclusion of self-LSP providers, and provisioning fan-out. Decision: provisioning fires on COMPONENT_ENABLED only (consistent with existing enable-time provider sync), not on install.
user-summary-candidate: When the coding-lsp component is enabled, the pi agent now automatically installs the pi-lens extension, which auto-discovers your installed language servers from PATH — so enabling a language (which installs its server) just works in pi with no extra setup. pi uses pi-lens for code intelligence instead of the generic LSP bridge.

technical-summary: Fixed opencode LSP key mismatch. coding-lsp's sync is language-keyed (e.g. 'python'), but opencode keys its lsp object by its own built-in server name ('pyright' for Python, 'clangd' for C++; 'typescript'/'rust' already match the language id). Kept coding-lsp generic and moved the mapping into the opencode adapter: added _LANGUAGE_TO_OPENCODE_KEY ({python: pyright, cpp: clangd}) plus _to_opencode_key/_to_language helpers. write_language_servers_opencode now writes under the opencode key, remove_language_servers_opencode resolves the language id to the opencode key before deleting, and read_language_servers_opencode maps opencode keys back to our language ids (languages absent from the map pass through unchanged). Without this, syncing Python produced a stray lsp.python entry instead of configuring opencode's built-in pyright server. Updated the opencode roundtrip test and added cpp->clangd mapping and typescript passthrough tests. Built-in keys confirmed from opencode docs. Follow-up to verify: whether the codex adapter ([language_servers.<name>]) needs the same internal mapping.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed opencode language-server config: Python now correctly configures opencode's built-in 'pyright' server (and C++ its 'clangd' server) instead of creating a mismatched 'python' entry. The LSP component stays language-agnostic; the opencode adapter maps to opencode's server names internally.

technical-summary: Surface lifecycle observer (_on_component_lifecycle) only branched on lifecycle.component.installed/uninstalled; the disabled and enabled events fired by disable_component/enable_component fell through silently, so disabling a component never pruned its managed surface blocks from instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, COPILOT.md, .clinerules, .roo). Mapped enabled->apply and disabled->prune+apply, paralleling installed/uninstalled. Root cause was masked because the integration suite (test_provider_surface_lifecycle.py) calls prune/apply directly to compensate for the absent event bus in test isolation, never exercising the observer event->action mapping. Added test_surface_observer_wiring.py covering all four lifecycle events plus the non-Path project_root guard.
user-summary-candidate: Disabling a component now removes its instruction blocks (e.g. ag-* tag doctrine) from AGENTS.md and other provider files, instead of leaving them stranded until uninstall.

technical-summary: Removed the redundant coding-lsp/usage surface contribution that duplicated the ag-lsp MCP tool list (lsp_symbols, lsp_diagnostics, etc.) into every provider's instruction file. The block was surfaced unconditionally to all providers, but the ag-lsp MCP server is only propagated to providers that don't self-provide LSP (opencode via native pyright language_servers_config, pi via on_lsp_enabled/pi-lens). This caused opencode's AGENTS.md to advertise lsp_* tools the agent didn't actually have, so the agent hunted for them, failed, and fell back to running pyright CLI. Root-cause fix: delete the contribution so the MCP registration is the single source of truth for tool availability — MCP delivers tool names and descriptions to the agent automatically via tools/list, and only to providers that actually receive the server. Usage doctrine remains in each MCP server's instructions field in coding-lsp.yaml. Regenerated provider surfaces (skill_surfaces apply), which pruned the coding-lsp/usage block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md. No gating mechanism and no native-LSP instruction block were added (chosen approach: omit). Providers unit suite green. Follow-up (not done): the ag-lsp-mgmt harness-instructions block is the same class of MCP-tool duplication and could be reconsidered; and lsp_mcp.py's FastMCP server does not currently pass the coding-lsp.yaml ag-lsp instructions field as server-level instructions.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed agents being told to use LSP tools (lsp_diagnostics, lsp_symbols) that aren't available to them. The LSP tool list is no longer duplicated into instruction files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md); agents discover LSP tools directly from the MCP server, so only agents that actually have the LSP server see those tools.

technical-summary: Replaced the per-block managed-surface fences with a single regenerated managed region per file. Previously each contribution was wrapped in its own <!-- AUDIAGENTIC:BEGIN <id> -->...<!-- AUDIAGENTIC:END <id> --> comment pair and matched/pruned by id. Now all of a file's managed blocks live inside one invisible boundary pair (<!-- ag:managed:begin -->...<!-- ag:managed:end -->) containing friendly `## Title` headings and a one-line managed notice; the region is regenerated wholesale on each apply. base.py: removed managed_block + prune_managed_blocks; added MANAGED_REGION_BEGIN/END/NOTICE constants, _REGION_RE, _LEGACY_BLOCK_RE, strip_managed_content(), render_managed_region(), and rewrote apply_managed_blocks() to strip prior region + legacy fences (auto-migration) then append the regenerated region (empty blocks remove the region). manager.py: prune_provider_surfaces now groups active blocks by path and calls apply_managed_blocks (region regeneration) instead of id-based prune_managed_blocks, so removed contributions drop out and files that lose all contributions are cleaned; dropped the prune_managed_blocks import. Block identity (block_id) is retained in the in-memory SurfaceBlock model (dedup, plan reporting) but is no longer emitted into files. Updated unit tests (region replacement, empty-removal, legacy migration, prune) and the consistency test (region regex + single-well-formed-region check + legacy-absence). Updated the Docker-gated integration helper managed_blocks_in to map region `## Title` headings back to contribution ids via load_surface_contributions. Regenerated all tracked agent surface files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COPILOT.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, .clinerules/audiagentic.md, .roo/rules/audiagentic.md) to the new region layout. Behavior note: managed content now consolidates into one contiguous region (moved to end of user-owned files on migration) rather than interleaving. Full unit suite passes.
user-summary-candidate: Managed sections in agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, etc.) are now wrapped in a single clean region with readable `## Title` headings and a 'managed by AUDiaGentic' notice, instead of noisy per-block <!-- AUDIAGENTIC:BEGIN/END --> comments around every entry. Old files migrate automatically on the next surface apply.

technical-summary: Stage 3 impl-scoped resolution layer. technical-summary: Fixed a foundation bug: the canonical error type _Error (AudiaGenticError) was a @dataclass(frozen=True) Exception. A frozen dataclass overrides __setattr__ to block all attribute writes, including __traceback__/__cause__/__context__ that Python's exception machinery assigns on raise and during propagation through contextlib with-blocks — producing FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field '__traceback__'. Exposed by the A26 work raising AudiaGenticError through rig contextmanager paths, but latent for all subclasses (LspError/LspServerError inherit the frozen __setattr__, hence their object.__setattr__ workarounds). Changed @dataclass(frozen=True) -> @dataclass(eq=False): exceptions are now mutable enough for the runtime to set traceback/cause/context, while eq=False keeps identity-based equality and hashability (the convention for exceptions; verified nothing hashes or value-compares errors). Verified: raise-through-contextmanager, raise-from chaining, LspError subclass, and __post_init__ code/kind validation all work. Also updated 5 stale assertions in test_embedded_launch.py from pytest.raises(SystemExit) to pytest.raises(AudiaGenticError) to match the A26-converted rig functions. Full tests/unit suite now green (only 2 environment-gated skips); the fix also cleared the workflow-propagation failures that were masked by the same FrozenInstanceError.

technical-summary: Fixed enable_component('coding-lsp') blocking/timing out. The coding-lsp enable lifecycle fires provision_provider_lsp_support, which runs each provider's on_lsp_enabled hook. The only such hook, pi adapter's _pi_ensure_lens, ran `pi install npm:pi-lens` (a network npm install) via subprocess.run with NO timeout, synchronously inside the MCP enable request. Since enable_component writes the enabled marker before firing the event, the component showed enabled while the MCP response blocked on npm, eventually hitting the client request timeout (MCP -32001). Fix: extracted the install into _install_pi_lens(pi_bin) (subprocess.run with timeout=300, logs non-zero/errors) and dispatched it on a background daemon thread from _pi_ensure_lens, which now returns immediately ({ok, started, detail}). Enabling no longer blocks on the install (best-effort, idempotent). Measured provision time dropped from 3.64s to 0.03s. Updated tests: split into test_ensure_lens_starts_background_install_when_harness_present (asserts non-blocking dispatch to _install_pi_lens with pi_bin) and test_install_pi_lens_runs_install_command (asserts the install command); skip-when-absent test unchanged. coding_lsp + providers unit suites green; Ruff clean. Not a bug (diagnosed for the user): the ag-lsp generic MCP is correctly projected only to providers that do NOT self-provide LSP (present in .mcp.json); native-LSP providers like opencode get native lsp config instead, which requires enabling a language.
user-summary-candidate: Enabling the LSP component no longer hangs/times out — the pi-lens extension install now runs in the background instead of blocking the request.

technical-summary: Fix two coding-lsp diagnostics bugs. (1) URI key mismatch: client URIs use Path.as_uri() (uppercase Windows drive, urllib encoding) while servers (pyright/pylsp) publishDiagnostics with lowercase drive / alt percent-encoding; state dicts (_diagnostics_cache, _opened_docs, _document_text, _last_change_version) keyed raw strings, so lookups missed and lsp_file_diagnostics silently returned [] / waited full timeout. Added pure-string LspSession._canonical_uri (decode, uppercase drive, re-quote) routed through did_open/did_change/sync_document/file_diagnostics/_sync_file_from_disk/_wait_for_publish/_on_publish_diagnostics. (2) workspace/diagnostic 30s timeout: diagnostics() sent the request unconditionally; pyright advertises diagnosticProvider.workspaceDiagnostics=false (no workspace pull) and never replies. Added _supports_workspace_diagnostic guard that fails fast with EXT-LSP-008 pointing to lsp_file_diagnostics; fixed has_capability('workspace/diagnostic') which checked wrong capability path (workspace.diagnostic) instead of top-level diagnosticProvider. Added tests for URI canonicalization, idempotency, and the capability guard.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed LSP diagnostics on Windows: single-file diagnostics no longer return empty due to drive-letter/URI casing mismatches, and workspace diagnostics fail fast with clear guidance instead of hanging 30s on servers (like pyright) that don't support workspace pull diagnostics.

technical-summary: coding-lsp workspace diagnostics + capability detection. CLI derived from server command (pyright-langserver→pyright, basedpyright-langserver→basedpyright), runs '<cli> --outputjson <root>', parses generalDiagnostics into the same {uri:[diagnostic]} shape (severity-string→LSP int, rule→code, canonical URI). Missing CLI / unknown server → fast EXT-LSP-004 pointing to file-diagnostics tools; timeout → EXT-LSP-003; unparseable → EXT-LSP-008. No new error codes. (2) Fixed has_capability: now reads top-level *Provider keys (definitionProvider, hoverProvider, …) instead of non-existent textDocument.*/workspace.* paths, so lsp_capabilities no longer reports []; an options object (even {}) counts as supported, explicit False/absent does not. (3) Earlier same-branch fixes retained: _canonical_uri URI normalization across all state dicts, and url2pathname-based _uri_to_path / uri_to_repo_relative replacing Path.from_uri (3.13-only; runtime is 3.12). Added unit tests for CLI fallback, missing-binary, batch-CLI mapping, capability detection, URI canonicalization, and 3.12 uri conversion. Fixed two stale pre-existing integration tests broken by the layering refactor (hook handler path optional/ removed; scaffold now seeds required ag-review prompt asset).

technical-summary: Sharded runtime feature state from the monolithic .audiagentic/config/runtime/features.yaml into per-component shards at .audiagentic/config/runtime/features/{parent}.yaml. set_component_state now writes only the affected parent's shard (atomic temp+rename), giving write-scope isolation so a mutation to component A never rewrites component B's data and removing the cross-component lost-update window. get_component_state reads the deterministic shard path with lazy read-migration: if a shard is absent but the legacy monolithic file exists, the parent's slice is extracted, nested->flat feature-key migration applied, and the shard written. Added migrate_to_shards(root) one-shot that splits every top-level key of the legacy file into shards (with per-shard flat migration) and renames the legacy file to features.yaml.migrated (never deleted, for rollback). load_feature_state/save_feature_state retained as back-compat whole-doc helpers that assemble/write across shards. No index file (deterministic shard paths via glob). No per-shard locking (out of scope; codebase relies on atomic replace). All public accessor signatures unchanged so the ~10 consumer files need no edits. Added migration test and isolation test. Validated host + inside Docker image audiagentic-test (12 foundation tests pass); provider+lsp unit suites green; ruff clean on changed files.
user-summary-candidate: Runtime feature state is now stored as one file per component instead of a single shared file, so enabling or configuring one component no longer rewrites every other component's saved settings. Existing single-file state is migrated automatically and the old file is preserved as a .migrated backup.

technical-summary: Fix orphaned MCP/LSP child processes leaking from harness host runs. Add foundation/system/supervised_process.supervised_run(): spawns the host then (Windows) assigns it to a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE so the kernel kills the whole descendant tree when the launcher dies (survives crash/hard-kill), forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM, and runs kill_process_tree in finally. Fix kill_process_tree POSIX branch which only SIGKILLed the single root pid despite its name — now enumerates transitive descendants via ps and kills deepest-first. Route pi and opencode real-run paths (previously plain subprocess.run with no host-tree teardown; opencode only reaped rig_pid) through supervised_run.

technical-summary: Live @github/GitHub-connector review turn against gpt-t1 hit EXT-GPTAUTO-002 (response-total-timeout, 3600s) with only 54 characters of assistant text, truncated mid-word. technical-summary: Two further live out-of-sequence-injection scenarios against fresh gpt-t1/gpt-t2 conversations both timed out (EXT-GPTAUTO-002) before the foreign-injection step was even reached in one case. E2 (gpt-t1): the trivial one-line baseline prompt itself never finished -- observation showed generating=true with stop-control visible for the full 3600s timeout, i.e. ChatGPT's own UI stayed in active-generation state indefinitely for a one-sentence reply. E3 (gpt-t2): the real turn timed out with completion-control visible but assistant-text-length=0 and an asymmetric observed-user-count=2 vs observed-assistant-count=3, suggesting the turn produced multiple internal assistant messages (plausibly a tool-call sub-message plus a final one) and the adapter's latest-assistant selection may have latched onto an intermediate/empty message rather than the true final reply -- a distinct, real edge case from the pure-stall cases, worth its own follow-up investigation separate from environmental throttling. In both cases the adapter behaved safely: chat-state settled to RECOVERING (not falsely completed, not silently stuck), tabs retained, no auto-resubmit, and the python process exited cleanly (0) with full diagnostics captured. Three consecutive real hour-long stalls across gpt-t1/gpt-t2 in one session (this @github review + these two) is a strong signal of either OpenAI-side throttling after heavy automated traffic or a project-level issue with these two test projects specifically -- not something further automated live retries will resolve; live testing against these two projects paused pending manual inspection.
user-summary-candidate: Found two more real GPT-auto stall patterns during live testing (one project stuck generating indefinitely on a trivial prompt, another producing multiple internal assistant messages per turn that may confuse response-matching) -- the adapter handled both safely with no stuck state or false completion, but paused further automated live testing since repeated real hour-long stalls suggest an account/project-level issue worth a manual look rather than more automated retries.

technical-summary: Gateway state audit (via agent_task_list_requests and agent_task_session_list) found real, pre-existing violations of the never-leave-non-terminal-state requirement, unrelated to today's live testing. 5 gpt-auto requests dated 2026-08-06 through 2026-08-10 are still persisted as state=running despite cancel-requested=true and watchdog-state=not-started -- cancellation was requested days ago and never reconciled to a terminal state. Separately, 6 more gpt-auto sessions dated 2026-08-12 through 2026-08-14 are still persisted as state=active despite runtime-state=stale-non-live (their owning process is long gone). This indicates the gateway's session/request bookkeeping has no sweep/reconciliation mechanism for abandoned records over time -- they simply accumulate as non-terminal indefinitely once their owning process exits without a clean close. This is distinct from and more systemic than any single bug found during live gpt-auto testing today; it affects the gateway's session/queue layer generally, not just the gpt-auto adapter.
user-summary-candidate: Found that the gateway leaves abandoned requests and sessions sitting in non-terminal states (running/active) indefinitely once their owning process exits without a clean close -- 5 requests cancelled 5-10 days ago never actually reconciled to a terminal state, plus 6 more sessions marked active despite being long-dead. This needs a proper sweep/reconciliation fix, not a one-off patch.

technical-summary: CORRECTION to the two earlier stall findings, after re-inspecting the real DOM directly (the user correctly pushed back that the tabs were not actually stuck). E1 (gpt-t1 @github review): the same assistant messageId that showed 54 chars at timeout now shows 23,995 chars -- it was genuinely still generating past the 3600s response-timeout-seconds, not stalled; this is a config-tuning gap (heavy @github/tool reviews can legitimately exceed 1 hour), not a detection bug. E2 (gpt-t1 trivial baseline): CONFIRMED real bug. The correct reply rendered almost instantly, but ChatGPT's own composer submit/stop toggle button (id=composer-submit-button, data-testid=stop-button, aria-label='Stop answering') never reverted from its 'stop' state -- still observably stuck hours later. turn.py's response-complete gating (`complete_satisfied = complete.satisfied and not current.generating`) treats this as an unconditional veto with no override path: response_stability_seconds (text-unchanged-for-N-seconds) is only consulted after complete_satisfied is already true, so a stuck generating=true blocks completion detection for the full response-timeout-seconds regardless of how long the text has been stable. Simultaneously-observed composer-editable=true (contradicting genuine active generation, which normally disables the composer) is a plausible corroborating override signal, not yet implemented pending review since this is the core completion-safety gate. E3 (gpt-t2): original diagnosis confirmed correct -- DOM now shows a transient empty assistant message followed by the real full answer, with message IDs differing from what was captured at timeout, confirming real message branching/multiplicity from the near-simultaneous real+injected sends.

technical-summary: Fixed the GP07 stuck-stop-control bug reproduced live 2026-08-15/16: turn.py's response-complete gate (complete_satisfied = complete.satisfied and not current.generating) and chat.py's _reconcile_unresolved_turn (if snapshot.generating: return False) both treated a raw generating/stop-control DOM signal as an unconditional veto over turn completion, so a stale ChatGPT composer button (proven to stick indefinitely after real completion) permanently blocked both live completion detection and unresolved-turn reconciliation. Formalized and implemented a corrected evidence model on GP07: generating/stop-control demoted to advisory-only (logged on disagreement via a new Tier-3-disagreement warning, never a veto); text-stability plus at least one corroborating any-of signal (completion-control OR a new message-finalized signal, [data-is-last-node], added to the local gpt-auto/gpt-auto-t1/gpt-auto-t2 provider workflow configs) is what actually proves completion. Added a new _reconciliation_evidence_clear() helper in chat.py, narrower-scoped than the existing provider_quiescent() (deliberately left unchanged -- it answers a different, more conservative 'safe to submit a new prompt' question). Fixed a real test-fixture gap found in the process: the shared snap() test helper set only the stop-control dom_signal, never the actual ChatSnapshot.generating field the production code reads, so no existing test had ever exercised the real bug path -- fixed and added three new deterministic regression tests (stuck-generating-still-completes, still-changing-text-still-blocks, reconciliation-despite-stuck-generating) plus live-validated end-to-end against a real gpt-t1 turn after a gateway restart.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a bug where gpt-auto could hang indefinitely (or fail to recover an interrupted conversation) whenever ChatGPT's own stop/submit button got stuck showing 'stop' after a response was actually done -- that button is no longer trusted alone; text stability plus another corroborating signal is what proves a turn is complete now.

technical-summary: Fixed a live-confirmed bug (GP07): gpt-auto's submission-proof phase used a single fixed deadline from observation-loop start rather than being activity-aware, so a long prompt (~7000 chars) that was genuinely typed, submitted, and actively generating was falsely reported as ambiguous/timed-out because the fixed ~15s clock expired before DOM proof was polled. Added a new shared, reusable observation state machine (observation_engine.py) designed after a real external design-review critique: evidence carries independent capabilities -- PROGRESS (authoritative content change; resets the inactivity clock, reopens a terminal candidate, recovers a stall), SOFT_LIVENESS (inferred UI widget state; grants one bounded lease extension, never a repeated reset, never authoritative -- closes a real infinite-hang hole a naive design would have had if widget evidence could indirectly block failure by repeatedly renewing the same lease), TERMINAL_WITNESS (corroborating; can enter/verify a candidate, cannot reopen one). A monotonic progress_generation counter makes candidate verification race-resistant (edge-triggered, not level-triggered -- an unchanged fact re-observed every poll does not re-count as new evidence). Outcomes distinguish 'proved failed' from 'failed to prove what happened' (UNRESOLVED_STALL vs a hard failure), closing a duplicate-submission risk on retry. Wired into turn.py's _await_submission_proof with two new config fields (submission-proof-progress-lease-seconds default 5min, submission-proof-absolute-ceiling-seconds default 15min); _await_response deliberately not yet rewired through the same engine (lower-risk-first, sequenced separately). Live-validated end-to-end against a real ChatGPT session with a long prompt; full deterministic gpt_auto/providers/agents test suites green.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a bug where gpt-auto could falsely report a long prompt submission as failed/ambiguous even though it had genuinely succeeded and was actively generating a response -- the timeout is now based on real activity (is anything still happening) instead of a fixed clock from when the check started.

technical-summary: Rewired gpt-auto's _await_response through the shared ObservationTracker engine (observation_engine.py, introduced for the submission-proof fix in the prior commit), replacing its previously-bespoke inline start/stall/total timer loop. Found and closed a real latent hole while doing so: response-active's any-of policy let stop-control/streaming-indicator/thinking-indicator widget transitions ALONE reset last_activity_at, so a flapping widget could indefinitely renew the response-wait stall clock even after stop-control was already demoted to advisory for completion detection itself (the earlier commit 7bd5643 only closed the completion-gate side of this, not the stall-timeout side -- both stemmed from the same underlying design gap). Widget transitions are SOFT_LIVENESS now (bounded grace, never a real reset); only genuine content change (new/changed assistant message) is PROGRESS and can indefinitely extend the wait. Outcomes distinguish BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (absolute ceiling) from a genuine stall, restoring the diagnostic granularity the old three-timer loop had. All pre-existing side effects preserved (state transitions, message-id publishing, ACTIVITY/IN_PROGRESS telemetry, the independent confirming re-snapshot before trusting a terminal candidate) -- verified by keeping the full gpt_auto suite green plus two new targeted regression tests, one of which (progress-emits-repeatedly-not-just-once) caught a real self-introduced mistake during this same rewiring where progress telemetry was accidentally suppressed after its first emission (would have starved the gateway's own watchdog activity lease). Removed the now-dead _fingerprint() helper. Live-validated against a real gpt-t1 turn after a gateway restart.
user-summary-candidate: Extended the earlier gpt-auto activity-lease fix to also cover response-completion detection, closing a related bug where a flapping ChatGPT UI widget could have indefinitely delayed the stall-timeout from ever firing even after the completion-detection side was already fixed.

technical-summary: PersistentChat.page_lost() no longer unconditionally reconciles (recreate-page + navigate-back) on every tab close. It now only does so when a turn is actively in flight (active_turn_id set); an idle chat losing its page moves to RECOVERING and waits for the existing lazy ensure_ready() -> reconcile() path on next real use, mirroring the idle/active distinction GptAutoProviderRuntime.recover() already applies one level up. Reproduced live with the user: closing an idle gpt-auto tab was immediately, unconditionally recreating itself every time with no way to leave it closed -- root cause traced to page_lost() calling reconcile() eagerly regardless of turn state.

technical-summary: Restarted the machine-scoped gpt-auto gateway to deploy tonight's fixes and live-validated three items: GP12's idle-tab-close fix (closed a test tab 5x over 15s, confirmed it never reopened, versus the pre-fix immediate unconditional reopen every time); GP11's composer-settle-wait and bounded-submit-retry fixes (3 sequential back-to-back turns on one session with zero settle gap, all completed cleanly with no composer-action-not-confirmed error); GP16 closed as superseded -- its root cause was already fixed under GP17, remaining scope was speculative future-proofing only.

technical-summary: Added ChatMessageRef and ChatSnapshot.message_refs: a single true-DOM-order sequence spanning both user and assistant messages, replacing two independently-filtered per-role querySelectorAll passes that could desync ids from texts and could never express cross-role interleaving order. The four legacy per-role arrays are now derived from this one unified pass for compatibility. Foundational slice for GP08's request-scoped correlation work.

technical-summary: GP25 live-validated: replaced turn.py's _matches()/_normal(), chat.py's _same_prompt()/_prompt_text_digest() with one shared PromptFingerprint/match_prompt() primitive tolerant of ChatGPT's Markdown-stripping DOM rendering (backticks, links, emphasis). Verified live end-to-end on gpt-auto-t1 with a prompt containing inline code, a Markdown link, and bold emphasis; completed cleanly with correctly-matched output.

technical-summary: GP30 live-validated: _await_response() now correlates against this request's own prompt-anchored message span (first assistant reply after the prompt, before the next user message of any provenance) instead of ChatSnapshot.latest_assistant_id/_text, which could be overwritten by a later, unrelated turn from any actor. Once established, identity is frozen for the turn; a conflicting later observation raises a clear error instead of silently following conversation-global-latest. technical-summary: Tracked GptAutoProviderRuntime.unregister_chat()'s previously fire-and-forget refresh_status_page() background task, and made ensure_dedicated_window_anchor() await any pending background tasks before issuing list_pages() on the shared CDP bridge -- closes a real, tested race where an untracked task could still be in flight when the next caller issued an unrelated bridge command. technical-summary: GptAutoConfig.from_project_dict() (added earlier tonight under GP20) merged a wrapped defaults.yaml payload against an unwrapped project settings dict without unwrapping both to the same shape first -- any caller passing an already-unwrapped bare settings dict (confirmed live: the gpt-auto live stress test harness) had every project override, including project-url, silently discarded in favor of defaults. technical-summary: Found and fixed a residual GP25 gap live: ChatGPT's renderer displays a fenced code block's language tag (e.g. the 'python' in ```python) as visible text rather than discarding it, which normalize_prompt_text() was stripping entirely, causing normalized submitted/observed text to permanently disagree on any prompt with a language-tagged fence. Fixed by keeping the language word, stripping only the backtick delimiters. Narrowed a real captured incident's char-count delta from 9 to 2 (the remaining 2 chars are a documented, distinct, deeper limitation around non-breaking-space re-encoding of code-block indentation, not yet fixed). Also added 'more-actions-menu' as a new advisory/diagnostic dom-signal (the end-of-turn action bar's overflow button) per a live suggestion -- not yet wired into any completion policy pending its own validation across multiple real completions.

technical-summary: GP27: built and ran a disposable-child-process crash-reproduction harness (zero shared-gateway/Brave risk) against the actual store.build_record/admit_record/claim_dispatch/bind_and_start_owned_attempt persistence choreography, crashing via os._exit() immediately after a durably-fsynced fake provider-side-effect -- the exact production incident's crash timing. GP18: got a strong new event-loop-ownership hypothesis (the singleton CdpClient's reader task may survive across pytest's per-test event loop teardown, becoming pending-forever rather than dead) from a live design consultation, with a concrete instrumentation plan for the next live cycle.
user-summary-candidate: Ruled out one possible cause of a rare data-loss bug in the automation gateway using a safe, isolated reproduction technique, and got a strong new lead on a separate CDP connection-hang bug.

technical-summary: ChatGPT removed the [data-is-last-node] DOM attribute that gpt-auto's message-finalized signal depended on. response-complete's evidence policy required message-finalized together with completion-control (all-of pairing from GP17), so this silently made completion detection permanently unsatisfiable -- live-reproduced as a full 600s hang despite the real ChatGPT turn having genuinely finished. Replaced message-finalized with more-actions-menu (an existing advisory signal, live-confirmed to co-occur with completion-control on real completions) in response-complete's all-of set, across the committed defaults.yaml and all three gitignored local provider configs that carry their own full policy copy. Validated read-only against the real production snapshot/policy code with zero new ChatGPT interaction: response-complete now correctly evaluates satisfied=True on an already-completed turn. Full deterministic suite (158 tests) passes.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a bug where gpt-auto could never detect that ChatGPT had finished responding, because ChatGPT changed its page markup and silently broke one of the two signals gpt-auto required together to confirm completion.

technical-summary: Generalized EvidencePolicy (foundation/workflow, provider-neutral) with any_of_groups: a disjunction of AND-groups layered on the existing flat all_of/any_of/none_of, so a corroborating-evidence requirement can have multiple independently-valid ways to be satisfied instead of one flat conjunction. Rewired gpt-auto's response-complete policy onto it (one live-validated group today) so a future DOM signal loss degrades to a surviving group instead of permanently blocking completion detection the way GP32 did. Deleted the dead message-finalized signal outright rather than keeping it as inert scaffolding. Separately, trimmed the three local .audiagentic/config/providers/gpt-auto*.yaml files to genuine sparse overlays (project-url only) against the packaged defaults.yaml -- they had been full byte-for-byte duplicates, which is exactly why GP32's fix needed four file edits instead of one. Found and fixed 6 call sites that read these config files directly via GptAutoConfig.from_dict() (bypassing the from_project_dict() merge path production code already used), including one always-running deterministic test that would have silently broken the moment the files were trimmed. Full gpt_auto + foundation/workflow deterministic suite (175 tests) passes; all three trimmed configs verified to resolve correctly through the real loader.
user-summary-candidate: Made gpt-auto's completion-detection logic resilient to future ChatGPT UI changes (it can now have multiple independent ways to confirm a response is done, not just one), and eliminated duplicated config across the three ChatGPT project configs so a future fix only needs to change one file.

technical-summary: Live-validated GP18's CDP self-healing reconnect (CdpClient._ensure_connected() detecting a dead reader task and forcing a fresh connection) and session-cache invalidation (PythonCdpBridge tracking connection_generation to drop stale Target.attachToTarget sessionIds after a reconnect) against the real gpt-auto-t1 ChatGPT account. Ran test_live_t1_scenarios end-to-end: a long-generation turn reached 39345+ characters and correctly completed via GP32's new any-of-groups response-complete policy, then a second scenario ran immediately after in the same session. Trace instrumentation confirms sub-3ms CDP command/response cycles throughout with zero recurrence of the original 30s hang or the -32001 'Session with given id not found' error GP18 targeted. A second scenario in the same run failed for an unrelated reason (composer submission timeout with a prompt-text mismatch, recorded separately as GP33) -- the CDP transport itself was proven healthy right up to that failure, ruling out GP18's mechanism as a cause.
user-summary-candidate: Confirmed live against the real ChatGPT account that the fix for the intermittent 30-second automation hang is working -- also found and logged a new, separate issue where submitting a second message right after a very long response can fail.

technical-summary: Live-reproduced (user directly observed a real ChatGPT tab appearing permanently stuck, no completion indicators) that ChatGPT's canvas/writing-block response rendering variant uses a completely different end-of-turn action bar (Edit/Copy/Open editor) than the standard chat-turn bubble GP32 validated -- completion-control and more-actions-menu were confirmed genuinely absent for a real canvas turn via the exact production DOM-scoping logic, making response-complete permanently unsatisfiable for that whole response variant, the same failure class as GP32 for a second variant. Added a second any-of-groups entry (canvas-edit-control + canvas-open-editor-control) to response-complete, exactly the resilience case the any-of-groups schema (built earlier the same night) was designed for. Because the local provider configs were trimmed to sparse overlays earlier tonight, this fix needed only one file edit instead of four. Validated read-only against the actual frozen turn with zero new ChatGPT interaction: response-complete now correctly evaluates satisfied.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a second variant of the same bug found earlier tonight: gpt-auto could get permanently stuck waiting for a response to finish when ChatGPT renders it in "canvas" mode, since that mode shows different completion buttons than the ones gpt-auto was checking for.

technical-summary: Fixed a genuine correctness/safety bug live-reproduced by direct user observation: gpt-auto's composer selector (document.querySelector('.ProseMirror')) is a first-match query with no scoping, and ChatGPT canvas/writing-block turns render their own .ProseMirror-based inline editor in the conversation history, positioned before the real chat composer in DOM order. Whenever any canvas turn existed anywhere in a conversation, this silently matched the canvas editor instead of the real composer -- causing prompt text to be typed into the wrong element, observed live as a composer-action-not-confirmed submission failure. Changed both the composer-presence check and the composer-typing target to document.querySelector('#prompt-textarea'), the real composer's stable unique id, confirmed present across every observed page state. Validated read-only against 5 live open ChatGPT tabs (several with canvas turns) -- the new selector resolves correctly in every case. Full deterministic suite (179 tests) passes.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a bug where gpt-auto could type a message into the wrong text box on the page whenever a prior response used ChatGPT's "canvas" writing mode, caught live when the user noticed the wrong box was being typed into.

technical-summary: Restored canonical numeric fallback error identity, aligned adapter-boundary analysis with public nested api/client modules, updated provider and incremental-ledger expectations, and completed non-GPT active-plan acceptance criteria.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed the reported non-GPT regressions and validated the unit, integration, and e2e gates; GPT-related planning records remain intentionally untouched.

technical-summary: Fixed every blocker a live gpt-auto-reviewer-agent code review found in tonight's earlier GP18/GP32/GP34/GP35 fixes. GP18: closed a session-generation TOCTOU race (CdpClient.command() gained required_generation, checked after _ensure_connected() and before send, raising a new CdpStaleGenerationError; PythonCdpBridge._session() now returns (session_id, generation) atomically and a new _session_command() helper retries once on staleness) and a concurrency race in _ensure_connected() (serialized under a new _connect_lock; removed a premature guard that prevented self-healing from a never-started state). Also: reader-task staleness now checks event-loop identity, not just .done(), and a reconnect re-issues Target.setDiscoverTargets so target lifecycle events don't silently stop. GP34: added a not-generating derived fact (from ChatSnapshot.generating) as a third required member of the canvas any-of-groups entry, since live monitoring proved the two canvas signals fire together at panel-creation time, not completion, giving no real independent corroboration on their own; removed them from turn.py's flat TERMINAL_WITNESS set since neither is a valid witness alone. GP38 (new): chat.py's unresolved-turn reconciliation accepted a single completion witness with no elapsed-time requirement, weaker than the main completion gate -- now reuses the same any-of-groups and enforces the same response_stability_seconds gap. EvidencePolicy: corrected an overstated resilience claim in its docstring and added matched_groups/missing_by_group diagnostics. Full deterministic suite (200+ tests) passes throughout.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed every real bug an independent code review found in tonight's ChatGPT-automation fixes: a rare connection race that could send a doomed request, a canvas-completion detection gap that could report a response as finished before it actually was, and a weaker recovery path that had the same gap with no safety margin at all.

technical-summary: message-finalized ([data-is-last-node]) was wrongly declared permanently removed by ChatGPT under GP32 earlier tonight, based on one long technical-essay response where it happened to be absent. Live-reproduced on a trivial single-paragraph answer during a basic-conversation smoke test: text fully rendered and stable for several minutes with completion-control and more-actions-menu genuinely absent from the entire document, while message-finalized was present and correctly scoped the whole time -- confirmed independently by the user inspecting the live DOM. The marker is conditional on the response's last block being a plain paragraph, not gone. Reinstated as a third any-of-groups entry on response-complete, paired with not-generating (not completion-control, since that never appearing at all is the gap this group covers) to avoid GP17's proven single-witness false-positive risk. chat.py's reconciliation path required no changes since it already reuses the shared any-of-groups.
user-summary-candidate: Restored a ChatGPT completion signal that was mistakenly thought to be gone -- it turns out to only appear for certain response types, and was needed to detect completion on simple short answers where the usual signals were slow to appear.

technical-summary: Hardened two fragile assumptions found via live user inspection of the real DOM. completion-control's selector was the same data-testid ChatGPT uses on both user-message and assistant-message action bars (confirmed live it can match the user's own prompt copy button, not the assistant's) -- added the assistant-specific aria-label="Copy response" as a second selector, giving a role-specific signal independent of scoping correctness. Separately, the assistantTurn container resolution used a fixed-depth parent walk (closest('article') || parentElement.parentElement) that only worked by coincidence of matching DOM depth in every conversation tested; two independent live DOM captures showed the correct container consistently carries a real class, .agent-turn -- now used as the primary scoping strategy, with the legacy chain kept as a fallback.
user-summary-candidate: Made gpt-auto's completion detection more robust: it now uses ChatGPT's own more specific labeling where available, instead of relying entirely on walking a fixed number of levels up the page structure.

technical-summary: GP42: scoped PythonCdpBridge's window-identity resolution to gpt-auto-relevant tabs only (via a new is_gpt_auto_relevant_url() covering chatgpt.com/chat.openai.com, the data: dashboard, and about:blank) instead of every tab on the shared browser, and added a single-target get_page bridge method (Target.getTargetInfo) so CdpBrowserController.page_by_handle() -- called on every poll tick of every open conversation via chat.py's snapshot() -- no longer triggers a full Target.getTargets enumeration of the whole shared browser on every call. technical-summary: Live GPT code review of GP42 (req_c4c7f7b3ac03444b) found a real merge blocker: PythonCdpBridge._refresh_page()'s except CdpError around Target.getTargetInfo forgot the handle/session on ANY CdpError, including transport-level failures (connection closed, client stopped, stale connection) -- not just a genuine CDP-server-confirmed 'no such target' response. This violated GP18's explicit invariant that _pages (handle->targetId identity) survives a WebSocket reconnect. Fixed by adding CdpProtocolError(CdpError), raised specifically where client.py's _read_loop receives a JSON-RPC error field from the CDP server itself (the only genuine positive evidence a target is gone); all other CdpError sites (stale connection, not connected, connection closed, client stopped) remain plain CdpError and now propagate uncaught through get_page rather than being misclassified as page destruction. Renamed the existing test to test_get_page_raises_and_forgets_handle_for_genuinely_closed_target (now using CdpProtocolError) and added test_get_page_preserves_handle_on_transport_failure proving a transport CdpError leaves _pages/_sessions untouched.

technical-summary: GP43: root-caused live (req_c4c7f7b3ac03444b, a 35850-char diff-heavy prompt) why agent_task_status stayed 'running' for ~12 minutes then surfaced a false submission-proof failure even though ChatGPT had fully and correctly answered. Byte-level diff against the real captured DOM text proved ChatGPT's renderer collapses horizontal-whitespace runs non-uniformly (a run of 9 plain spaces observed collapsed to a single \xa0), not the simple 1:1 NBSP substitution the module's own docstring had assumed and left as an open gap. Fixed normalize_prompt_text() to normalize \xa0 to a plain space and collapse any run of 2+ horizontal-whitespace characters to one, verified to produce a byte-for-byte match against the real live-captured data. Case sensitivity and indentation presence (vs absence) remain significant; only exact interior-whitespace run length is no longer compared, which is the correct tradeoff since this primitive only needs to correlate content, not formatting fidelity.

technical-summary: GP44: root-caused live why req_42f9580ebfcd45d6 (a real, currently-in-flight request) was stuck indefinitely at state=running with zero recorded attempts, despite the underlying ChatGPT conversation being genuinely complete. Fixed normalize_prompt_text() to also collapse any run of 2+ newlines to one; verified byte-for-byte against the real live-captured incident data.

technical-summary: Hardened provider activity watcher shutdown: stop checks before relaying queued lines and blocking joins complete before WorkerResultEnvelope. user-summary-candidate: Idle agent sessions now release their live browser or harness after 30 minutes without new work, while the next message can automatically reopen the same durable provider conversation when supported.
